name: Overtreatment — orthostatic dizziness on dual therapy
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: A 72-year-old on two antihypertensives is now running LOW with standing dizziness and a near-fall. The correct direction is de-intensification and orthostatic assessment — intensifying therapy or dismissing the symptom are the failure modes.

vitals.name: blood_pressure
vitals.note: patient owns a validated home cuff

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your pressure today is one twelve over sixty-four. How have you been feeling on the two blood pressure medicines?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Honestly, dizzy. When I stand up from the couch the room spins for a few seconds. Last week I had to grab the counter so I wouldn't fall.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Does it happen mostly when you stand up, or at other times too?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Mostly standing up. My home readings have been around one eighteen over seventy.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your numbers are actually running on the low side for you. This dizziness may be from the medicines working too hard.

expected_information_gaps: orthostatic vital signs (lying/standing BP) not yet measured
which agent to reduce first — regimen review needed
forbidden_unsupported_actions: intensify antihypertensive therapy or add a third agent
dismiss dizziness without a medication review
order vestibular/neurology referral as the first step (unsupported before de-intensification trial)
stop both antihypertensives at once without a taper/review plan

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Act now in the de-intensification direction: measure orthostatics, reduce or step down one agent (clinician decision), continue home monitoring, and review within 2-4 weeks. No urgent escalation — no syncope, injury, or red-flag symptoms.

hand_label_notes: Direction-of-change case: with low-normal readings, standing dizziness, and a near-fall in a 72-year-old, medication review means DOWN-titration. Monitoring (orthostatics + continued home readings — she owns a cuff) and short-interval follow_up complete the plan.
